content:
There are no universally applicable templates that must be compulsorily submitted to a referendum without requiring signature collection across all jurisdictions (e.g., countries, states, or local governments). Referendum rules—including whether petitions or signature requirements are needed—are established by each governing body or legal system.

In some places, certain types of referendums (e.g., constitutional amendments, major tax changes, or specific policy initiatives) may be exempt from signature requirements and submitted directly to the electorate by legislative or executive authorities. Other referendums may always require petition signatures before appearing on the ballot.

To provide a precise answer, please specify the country, region, or governing body you are referring to.
